finding.claim: notifyAll fetches attacker-supplied callback URLs server-side with no validation, enabling blind SSRF (POST with server-side payload to internal hosts/IPs every minute).
finding.source: callbackUrl parameter of subscribe() (src/Jobs.java:13), received from POST /subscribe per comment at line 12, stored unchanged at line 14.
finding.sink: client.send(req, ...) at src/Jobs.java:24, request URI built from URI.create(cb) at src/Jobs.java:21.

trace.note: Comment documents POST /subscribe body containing callbackUrl.
subscribe() accepts callbackUrl as a String parameter.
callbackUrl stored unvalidated in static subscriptions map.
Comment: notifyAll runs every minute, so stored URLs are fetched repeatedly without further attacker action.
Iterates over all stored callback values.
URI.create(cb) converts attacker string into the request target.
POST body is server-side payload; attacker does not control body here.
client.send issues the request from the server's network position; response body discarded, so blind.

finding.guards_checked: No host, IP, port, or private-range allowlist; no DNS resolution check. Scheme is implicitly limited to http/https by java.net.http (file: and others rejected). HttpClient.newHttpClient() default Redirect.NEVER, so redirect-based pivot from public host is blocked, but direct internal targets remain reachable. Authentication on /subscribe is not verifiable from this repo (only src/Jobs.java exists, not a git repo); if /subscribe is admin-only, severity drops but missing validation stands.

verdict.guard_found: none: no host, IP, port, or scheme check between URI.create(cb) at src/Jobs.java:21 and client.send at src/Jobs.java:24; the only validation in the file is the regex in thumb() at src/Jobs.java:30, which is not on this path.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches the file (comment at src/Jobs.java:12, storage at :14, URI.create at :21, send at :24), and no closing guard exists on the path, but the only evidence that callbackUrl comes from a remote caller is the comment at src/Jobs.java:12, and the repo contains no /subscribe handler, so whether an unauthenticated or low-privilege attacker can reach it cannot be decided.

finding.claim: Not a finding: thumb() is allowlisted. Regex https://cdn\.example\.com/img/[a-z0-9]+\.png with String.matches (full match) pins host to cdn.example.com and excludes @ # / \ : ?, so no userinfo, fragment, or path tricks; redirects disabled by default Redirect.NEVER.
finding.sink: client.send at src/Jobs.java:34 via URI.create at src/Jobs.java:33

trace.note: Full-match regex validation pins host to cdn.example.com.
URI.create on validated string; grammar cannot diverge from validator.

finding.guards_checked: Full-string regex anchoring, literal escaped host and extension, restricted character class, Redirect.NEVER default.

verdict.guard_found: src/Jobs.java:30 `src.matches("https://cdn\\.example\\.com/img/[a-z0-9]+\\.png")` is a full-string anchored match with the host and scheme pinned as literals. The character class `[a-z0-9]+` excludes `@`, `#`, `/`, `\`, `:`, `?`, `.` and `%`, so no userinfo, fragment, query, or extra path segments can get through. src/Jobs.java:33 `URI.create` only sees strings that already passed this check. src/Jobs.java:10 `HttpClient.newHttpClient()` uses the default redirect policy, which is NEVER, so 34 does not follow redirects.
verdict.reason: The trace at src/Jobs.java:29-34 matches the code, and the anchored full-string regex at src/Jobs.java:30 pins scheme, host, and a restricted path, so the attacker-supplied `src` cannot reach an arbitrary host (SSRF) and the default no-redirect client at src/Jobs.java:10 closes the redirect route.
